pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these should a good county sketch map have? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of a tractor
   B. A title
   C. A photograph of the teacher
   D. A recipe

2. A pupil says that a county with many people must be the biggest in area. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Area and population are different things
   B. Counties never have people
   C. People make land bigger
   D. Only farms make counties big

3. On a physical map, what colour is often used for high mountains? (1 mark)
   A. Brown
   B. Pink
   C. Blue
   D. White

4. Which of these is a way of caring for a river? (1 mark)
   A. Planting trees along its banks
   B. Cutting trees at the bank
   C. Throwing rubbish into it
   D. Washing cars in it

5. What is a river? (1 mark)
   A. Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   B. A big lake
   C. A steep hill
   D. A flat plain

6. Why does Kenya not have summer and winter like countries far from the equator? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya is too small
   B. Kenya has no rain
   C. Kenya has no sun
   D. Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little

7. Why was Fort Jesus built? (1 mark)
   A. To make sugar
   B. To keep cattle
   C. To grow food
   D. To guard the harbour

8. Which place in Nairobi shows traditional homes and dances of many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Fort Jesus
   B. Bomas of Kenya
   C. Lamu Old Town
   D. Gede Ruins

9. Gede Ruins are near which coastal town? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Watamu
   C. Nakuru
   D. Nyeri

10. Who built Fort Jesus? (1 mark)
   A. The British in 1950
   B. Nobody built it
   C. The Kenyan government in 1990
   D. The Portuguese

11. What is the difference between a museum and a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   B. A cultural centre has no dances
   C. There is no difference
   D. A museum is always outdoors

12. What is harambee? (1 mark)
   A. A school subject
   B. A kind of market
   C. Working together to solve a problem
   D. A type of crop

13. What is one benefit of interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. We become poor
   B. We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   C. We stop trading
   D. We stop working

14. Who brings medicine and equipment to hospitals? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody
   B. Drivers and traders
   C. Only teachers
   D. Only farmers

15. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a nurse give? (1 mark)
   A. Health care
   B. Learning
   C. Transport
   D. Food

16. Who helps at weddings and funerals in many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Neighbours and relatives
   B. Only the government
   C. Only the police
   D. Nobody

17. What do we call an area where many people live close together? (1 mark)
   A. Wild
   B. Sparsely populated
   C. Densely populated
   D. Empty

18. Which of these economic activities is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A fish
   B. A stone
   C. Teaching
   D. A crop of maize

19. What is an economic activity? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A holiday
   C. A game after school
   D. Work done to earn income or make goods and services

20. What does jua kali mean in Kiswahili? (1 mark)
   A. Big factory
   B. Rainy day
   C. Hot sun
   D. Cold wind

21. What is one problem that industries can cause? (1 mark)
   A. More rain
   B. Less trade
   C. Fewer jobs
   D. Pollution

22. Where are fish processing factories found? (1 mark)
   A. In a desert without water
   B. On the shores of Lake Victoria
   C. On top of Mount Kenya
   D. In the sky

23. Which town is Kenya's main port and a busy industrial town? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Mombasa
   C. Nyeri
   D. Kericho

24. What does the project manager do? (1 mark)
   A. Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   B. Prints books
   C. Drives the bus
   D. Cooks lunch

25. Which is not a good reason to choose a project? (1 mark)
   A. It is wanted
   B. We have the skills
   C. It is dangerous but exciting
   D. It is safe

26. Which of these can be a school enterprise project? (1 mark)
   A. A war
   B. A robbery
   C. Bullying
   D. A vegetable garden

27. Which of these helps drivers to see pupils on the road? (1 mark)
   A. Reflective strips
   B. A hat that covers the eyes
   C. A black bag
   D. Dark clothes

28. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. Money left after paying all costs
   B. The price of a book
   C. All the money spent
   D. Money borrowed

29. Which action shows respect? (1 mark)
   A. Insulting classmates
   B. Ignoring teachers
   C. Breaking desks
   D. Greeting teachers politely

30. Being good even when nobody is watching is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Fashion
   B. Punishment
   C. Integrity
   D. Boasting

31. When talking about a conflict, which kind of sentence is best? (1 mark)
   A. I will hit you
   B. Everyone hates you
   C. You are stupid
   D. I felt hurt when...

32. What should you do if you are very angry? (1 mark)
   A. Hit someone
   B. Break something
   C. Walk away and calm down
   D. Shout insults

33. Which law forbids child labour and FGM in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Only a poster
   B. Only school rules
   C. Nothing forbids it
   D. The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act

34. Which school transport is safe? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger's car
   B. A vehicle approved by school and parents
   C. An overloaded vehicle
   D. A vehicle with no seats

35. Which is an effect of child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Better health
   B. Fear and lost education
   C. Higher marks
   D. More friends

36. Which shows respect for the minority? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at them
   B. Ignoring them
   C. Listening to those who did not win
   D. Sending them away

37. What should a Children's Government NOT do? (1 mark)
   A. Punish other pupils by itself
   B. Welcome visitors
   C. Organise clean-up days
   D. Represent pupils

38. Who writes down what is discussed and decided at a meeting? (1 mark)
   A. The secretary
   B. The Speaker
   C. The president
   D. The patron

39. Which of these is a county government service? (1 mark)
   A. Running the army
   B. Running county health centres
   C. Defending the country
   D. Issuing passports

40. Who approves the governor's choice of county executive committee members? (1 mark)
   A. The county assembly
   B. The village elder
   C. The teachers
   D. The chief

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how to draw a dot map showing population distribution in your county. (4 marks)

42. Explain the difference between the governor and the president. (3 marks)

43. Explain the meaning of population distribution. (2 marks)

44. What is a compass used for? (2 marks)

45. Name four roles in a school enterprise team and state one duty for each. (4 marks)

46. Explain what harambee is and give one example of what it can be used for. (2 marks)

47. Give two traditional foods and say where each is popular. (4 marks)

48. Explain the meaning of a good citizen in school. (2 marks)

49. Give two reasons why we obey school rules. (2 marks)

50. Explain three ways in which a county can benefit when its officers know its size and location well. (3 marks)

51. Name the four seasons in the county. (2 marks)

52. Give four school rules and one reason for each. (4 marks)

53. Explain what an industry is. (2 marks)

54. A pupil stands facing east. Say what is behind the pupil, on the left and on the right. (3 marks)

55. The sugar factory employs 700 workers and the tea factory employs 400 workers. How many workers are there in the two factories together? Show your working. (3 marks)

56. Explain how pollution can be reduced in an industry. (3 marks)

57. How do you calculate profit? (2 marks)

58. Match each activity to a resource it uses: fishing, farming, mining, tourism. (4 marks)

59. Name two water features found in Kenya. (2 marks)

60. Explain how the four seasons can influence what people do in your county. Give one example for each season. (5 marks)

61. Name two places where you can find information about your school's history. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — A title
   A good map has a title, a north arrow and a key.

2. A — Area and population are different things
   Size is about area. Population is the number of people.

3. A — Brown
   Brown shows high land such as mountains.

4. A — Planting trees along its banks
   Trees hold the soil and keep the water clean.

5. A — Water flowing along a channel from high land to low land
   Rivers flow along channels towards a lake or an ocean.

6. D — Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little
   Near the equator the temperature stays fairly steady, so rain and altitude decide our seasons.

7. D — To guard the harbour
   It was built as a stone fort to guard the harbour.

8. B — Bomas of Kenya
   The Bomas of Kenya is a cultural centre in Nairobi.

9. B — Watamu
   Gede Ruins are near Watamu in Kilifi County.

10. D — The Portuguese
   The Portuguese built the fort more than 400 years ago.

11. A — A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   Cultural centres let visitors see and take part in living culture.

12. C — Working together to solve a problem
   Harambee means pulling together.

13. B — We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   Sharing skills gives us more goods and services.

14. B — Drivers and traders
   Transport workers carry goods to hospitals.

15. A — Health care
   Nurses give health care.

16. A — Neighbours and relatives
   People help by cooking, lending items and comforting.

17. C — Densely populated
   Dense means crowded.

18. C — Teaching
   Teaching is work done to help others.

19. D — Work done to earn income or make goods and services
   Economic activities bring in income.

20. C — Hot sun
   Jua kali means hot sun, from workers who work outdoors.

21. D — Pollution
   Waste from factories can pollute air and water.

22. B — On the shores of Lake Victoria
   Fish are processed near the lake where they are caught.

23. B — Mombasa
   Mombasa is Kenya's main port.

24. A — Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   The manager coordinates the work.

25. C — It is dangerous but exciting
   A project must be safe for children.

26. D — A vegetable garden
   A garden can be run safely by pupils.

27. A — Reflective strips
   Reflective strips shine in light.

28. A — Money left after paying all costs
   Profit = income - costs.

29. D — Greeting teachers politely
   Polite greetings show respect.

30. C — Integrity
   Integrity means doing right when unseen.

31. D — I felt hurt when...
   'I' sentences share feelings without blaming.

32. C — Walk away and calm down
   Cooling down prevents harm.

33. D — The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act
   Kenyan law protects children.

34. B — A vehicle approved by school and parents
   Approved vehicles are safer.

35. B — Fear and lost education
   Abuse harms the child's life.

36. C — Listening to those who did not win
   Democracy includes everyone.

37. A — Punish other pupils by itself
   Only teachers decide on discipline.

38. A — The secretary
   The secretary keeps the minutes.

39. B — Running county health centres
   Health centres are a county responsibility.

40. A — The county assembly
   The assembly must approve them.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county boundary. Decide how many people one dot stands for. Put more dots where more people live and fewer dots where few live. Add a title and key.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The president leads the national government of the whole country. The governor leads one county government.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is how the people are spread out over an area, showing where many people live and where few live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for spread of people, 1 mark for many and few.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: A compass is used to find direction. Its needle points to north.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for finding direction, 1 mark for the needle pointing north.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Project manager leads the team, treasurer keeps money records, production team makes the goods, sales team sells the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role and duty pair.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Harambee is people pulling together to solve a problem, for example to build a school or a clinic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: githeri in central Kenya and fish with ugali near Lake Victoria. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food and 1 mark for each correct place.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: A good citizen in school follows the rules, respects others and does what is good for the whole school community.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rules/respect, 1 mark for the community idea.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rules keep everyone safe and they help everyone to learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: They can plan roads and health centres to reach people. They can share resources with neighbours. They can plan journeys and services better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hot, cold, dry and rainy.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for all four, 1 mark for two or three.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Come on time to avoid missing lessons; keep the school clean for health; respect others for peace; care for property so it lasts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule with a reason.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: An industry is a place or business where raw materials are made into goods, or where a service is given to many people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making goods, 1 mark for services or raw materials.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind is west. On the left is north. On the right is south.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,100 workers.
   Working / marking points: 700 + 400 = 1,100. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for correct sum, 1 mark for the unit.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Treat waste before releasing it, plant trees, and use clean machines or methods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Profit is found by subtracting the costs from the income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for costs from income.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fishing uses lakes or ocean, farming uses land and soil, mining uses minerals, tourism uses wildlife or beaches.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lake Victoria and the Tana River. Accept Lake Turkana, Lake Naivasha or the Indian Ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct feature.

60. (5 marks)
   Answer: Rainy: farmers plant crops. Dry: farmers harvest and dry crops. Hot: people drink more water and wear light clothes. Cold: people wear warm clothes and drink hot tea. Award a fifth mark for a clear explanation of why seasons matter for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each season example and 1 mark for the link to activities.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: The headteacher or teachers, and the school records or log book. Accept old photographs or elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each source.
